newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - CFDs fall again, mogas up $.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - CFDs fall again, mogas up $.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Monday. Gasoline edged slightly higher but Brent CFDs were lower and fuel was little changed after recovering early losses.
Gasoline swaps firmed $1 a tonne to traded at $193.25 for the balance of April and between $195 and $196 for May. Crack spreads also made modest gains after hitting lows on Thursday of last week.
"We were struggling to find offers," said a broker.
He saw bids at $4.20 a barrel, $3.10, $3.45 and $4.40 on the third, fourth, first and second quarters respectively.
Brent CFDs remained depressed, drifting five cents lower for this week and a couple lower for next.
This week talked either side of $1 a barrel below June while next week traded at 73 cents under.

Inter-week contango traded at 10 cents for next week against the following week. The inter-week contango now looks 26 cents between this and next week, then 10 cents, 7 cents and 9 cents for the next consecutive three inter-week periods.

The deep contango on CFDs reflects the bearish mood among many physical crude oil traders. They expect growing supply of sour crude oil from Iraq in the second quarter and renewed difficulty in selling Brent to the U.S.
Heavy fuel swaps were little changed by the close after recovering an early dip of $1 a tonne.
"We were back to $84 to $84.50 in the afternoon but it was very quiet with only a handful of deals," said a broker.
April barges were pegged around $84.50 with May at $85.25 by late afternoon. April cargoes traded at $83 while the Mediterranean traded at $80 in april and between $77 and $78 in May.
Traders said middle cuts of the barrel were unchanged but very quiet.

Jet premiums held around $24 a tonne above the IPE for April and $25 above for May. The third quarter was $27.50 above and the fourth $33 above. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
